Tooltip_craft_YoghurtIncubatorDesc: A Lidded Clay Pot wrapped in cloth. Pour in scalded milk (20 minutes at 85°C: a Stone Hearth's cauldron, or a pot on a lit stove or fire) and add a yogurt or a starter; it sets by itself once the milk has cooled to 45°C. Pour from a cauldron within 2 tiles, or carry the milk over hot, best in a Wrapped Clay Pot. Or put kefir grains in and pour any milk under 45°C onto them for kefir.
Tooltip_craft_StarterCultureCrockDesc: A ceramic jar or pot under a cloth, for growing a yogurt starter from wheat and milk when no yogurt is left to start from. It loads with milk at 35 to 45°C, from a Stone Hearth's cauldron or a Wrapped Clay Pot, or with soured milk alone. Small enough to stand on a counter or table, or on the floor.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Yog: A wide lidded pot that holds 5 litres. Wrap it in cloth to build a Culturing Pot, or in a sheet to carry hot milk.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Jar: Home-set yogurt: a glass jar holds 1 L, a ceramic jar 2.5 L. Eat it from the jar a 250 ml portion at a time, or spoon portions into Empty Yogurt Containers; the jar comes back with the last spoonful.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Act: A live culture grown on wheat. Add it to a Culturing Pot to set one batch.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Emp: Wash it and fill it again with home-set yogurt.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Wra: Carries 5 litres of scalded milk and keeps it hot: about 15°C lost in an hour, where an open pot loses it in minutes. Unwrap it when empty.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Sal: Butter worked with salt, as storage butter was packed. Keeps about three months in a cellar, longer in a fridge or the cold, about six weeks in a warm room.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Cla: Butter cooked until its water is gone and the clear fat strained off its milk solids. Like Lard, it never goes off.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Bur: Clarified butter left on the heat too long. Scrape Out Burnt Butter to get the pot or saucepan back.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Kef: A sachet of dried kefir grains. Open it for 10 grains.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Dri: Kefir grains dried to keep. Two batches in milk bring them back to life.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationDairy_Kef: Kefir grains: a gram each, about 40 ml of milk a grain. They grow with every good batch. Out of milk they go hungry in about 2 days and die in about 7 at 20°C, slower in a fridge. Spread them on a cloth to dry them for keeping.
Kefir grains drying on a cloth where it is left: about 2 days at 25°C, 5 at 10°C, never in a shut room (open a window). Dry, collect them as Dried Kefir Grains and the cloth comes back.
